cities.d: (Sinhala: කොළඹ; Tamil: கொழும்பு) — commercial capital and the largest city of Sri Lanka. Hotels, cafés, restaurants, night clubs and shopping.

x.around: The Sri Lankan Tourist Development Authority also operates its own fleet of 'tuk-tuks' around Colombo which are tourist friendly and metered to ensure that travellers are aware of the price being paid. Tourist board tuk tuks are distinguishable by their unique paintings. These three-wheelers can be booked 24 hours a day by calling 0712 500 800 or 0772 299 299.

hidden.d: Mosque founded by C.W.W. Kannangara Mawatha.

It is the meeting place for the Masonic Lodges. It was built in 1901 during British rule and designed by E. Skinner, an associate of the Royal Institute of British Architects, and built by the Colombo Commercial Company.
This museum features Sri Lanka's floral and fauna in dioramas.
Hindu temple in Colombo 10. Devoted to Shiva and Ganesh.
Hindu temple in Colombo 13
The church plays an important role within the history of the Church Missionary Society on the island.
It was dedicated on 29 September 1887 and is a landmark in Kollupitiya, a suburb of Colombo, the commercial capital of Sri Lanka. A magnificent building of stone, mortar and wood.

n.en: St Michael and All Angels Anglican Church

hidden.d: It was founded in the late 19th century, and prospered during the colonial and post-colonial periods, it was a centre for the Scots element in Colombo, the capital city of what was then Ceylon.

x.intro: Colombo (Sinhala: කොළඹ, Tamil: கொழும்பு) is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka, and still perceived by many as the capital though the suburb of Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is now the official capital. Just like any other big South Asian city, Colombo is congested, noisy, busy, and vibrant with a mixture of modern life and colonial architecture. It is the financial centre of the island and a popular tourist destination.

must.d: Department of National Museums. Also known as the Sri Lanka National Museum, it is the largest museum in Colombo. Among its exhibits, it contains regalia of the 17th-century Kandyan kings.
Distinctive Colombo telecommunications tower that offers great views. At night, it is shining with the colours on the flower changing every few seconds.
This historic mosque is a popular tourist site. Jami-Ul-Alfar Mosque was built in 1909 by the Pettah Muslim community to fulfill their required five-times-daily prayer and Jummah on Fridays.
One of the most important temples in Colombo. The temple's architecture is an eclectic mix of Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian and Chinese styles.
The seat of the archbishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Colombo in Sri Lanka.
One of the oldest churches built during the Dutch era in 1749. The interior is decorated with Dutch furniture with the wooden carved pews, chairs, pulpit and lecterns.
Nice but very small museum documenting Dutch colonial rule in Sri Lanka. Houses Dutch-inspired artifacts.
A Roman Catholic church with basilica status. The church is home to the venerated statue of Our Lady of Lanka.

n.de: Basilika Unserer Lieben Frau von Lanka
n.en: Basilica of Our Lady of Lanka
n.es: Santuario y Basílica de Nuestra Señora de Lanka
n.it: basilica of Our Lady of Lanka

next.d: 120 km (less than 4 hours away) outside of Colombo. Kandy is a small, tranquil town that holds the sacred tooth of Buddha, a sacred relic of the Buddhist faith.
160 km northeast of Colombo, is a very important Buddhist site in Sri Lanka. The remains of the ancient fortress and city date back to 477 AD.
beach town just north of the airport, also famous for its canals and fish market. It used to be a backpacker haven, though it's more and more becoming a resort with new expensive hotels being built.

x.safe: Colombo is like most other South Asian capitals. Although it is not as dangerous as one would think, tourists should be very vigilant. Many first time visitors to Colombo find themselves falling victim to scams and touts; however, seasoned visitors to Sri Lanka are rarely scammed and it is very simple to avoid being a victim of scammers as long as you take precautions such as

cities.d: (Sinhala: ශ්‍රී ජයවර්ධනපුර කෝට්ටේ; Tamil: ஶ்ரீ ஜெயவர்த்தனபுர கோட்டை) — also known as Kotte, new capital of Sri Lanka

x.intro: Sri Jayawardenapura Kotte (Sinhalese: ශ්‍රී ජයවර්ධනපුර කෝට්ටේ; Tamil: ஶ்ரீ ஜெயவர்த்தனபுர கோட்டை) (also known as Kotte) is the capital city of Sri Lanka. In practice, it is a suburb of Colombo, which completely surrounds it. Over 100,000 people live in Kotte itself.

cities.d: (Sinhala: අනුරාධපුරය; Tamil: அனுராதபுரம்) — ruins of ancient capitals (partially restored). UNESCO World Heritage Site.

x.around: Tuk tuks and buses are abundant. The PickMe app is the ridesharing app of choice here, for motorbikes, tuk tuks and taxis. The New Town is relatively small, and can be walked from one end to another in half an hour.

hidden.d: A monastery site of Theravada Buddhism.
The second most sacred place in Sri Lanka, after the Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth) in Kandy and also part of the eight sacred places in Sri Lanka.
The oldest and most voluminous stupa at Anuradhapura, has been fully restored, painted white, and is a centre of worship.
Large stupa (Buddhist worship structure. Also known as "Dagoba"), undergoing restoration work. Part of the Jetavana Monastery.

The 1,600 stone pillars that we see today are what are left of an enormous building. Also called the Brazen Palace, this nine-storey monastery was once home to a thousand monks, whose duties included tending the sacred Bo tree,…

x.intro: Anuradhapura is a UNESCO World Heritage listed city in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka.
x.safe: Beware of the monkeys. Monkeys, particularly macaques (small, red-faced monkeys) can get quite aggressive, and have been known to steal unattended personal belongs.

cities.d: (Sinhala: මඩකලපුව; Tamil: மட்டக்களப்பு) — a city built on a lagoon. Beautiful shallow beaches, paddy fields, historical places.

x.around: The old town is very compact, so is easily walkable. Tuk-tuks are available, but agree on a price before departing. A rule of thumb is Rs. 100 per kilometre. Also, public Sri Lankan Transport Board buses and private bus/van service are available.

hidden.d: This is a popular Hindu shrine, where an annual pilgrimage occurs during July/August.
The Batticaloa Gate is a monument commemmorating the former port which connected the old town on the island of Puliyanthivu (island) with the mainland.
This neo-Gothic cathedral is the main Catholic church in Batticaloa diocese.

This bridge was built in 1924 during British colonial rule. The bridge was named Lady Manning Bridge in honour of the wife of William Manning, the British Governor of Ceylon. It was the oldest and longest iron bridge in Sri Lanka.

This fort was built by the Portuguese in 1628 and was the first to be captured by the Dutch in 1638. Later, the fort was used by the British from 1745. It now contains government administration offices.
Guided trail rides and horsemanship sessions in the Punanai countryside. Advance reservation and rider-suitability review are required.

x.intro: Batticaloa (Tamil: மட்டக்களப்பு, Sinhala: මඩකලපුව) is a city (pop. 86,227 in 2012) in Northeastern Sri Lanka, known for its lagoon, historical landmarks and nearby beaches.

next.d: about 85 km south from Batticaloa, is a popular surfing and tourist destination. Two daily direct buses at 06:00 and 10:00. Rs. 135, 5-6 hours. Stops for 1 hour in the town of Akuraivili.
west of Batticaloa, is an ancient capital city of Sri Lanka and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site. It has ruins and bird- and elephant-watching places.

cities.d: (Sinhala: ගාල්ල; Tamil: காலி) — famous Dutch fort. Host city of the Galle Literary Festival. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

x.around: Tuk Tuk or on foot is your best bet if you are traveling in Galle or close by. The Old Town of Galle and its fortifications are within walking distance from the central bus station, so it's better to walk rather than to take a tuk-tuk.

hidden.d: Anglican Church.
A walk here at sunset is very pleasant if you don't mind being hassled to buy table cloths, fake antique 'Dutch' coins, or powdered milk.
Found: 1892.
Beach club with great vibe and excellent drinks. Bring your towel and enjoy the day there.
Look inside.

x.intro: Galle is in the Southern Province of Sri Lanka. Galle's old town with its fortifications have been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

must.d: It is housed in the old Dutch East India Company VOC Warehouse in Galle Fort.

next.d: 5 km to the southeast on Route A2. A beautiful beach for swimming. Many places to eat. Buses run every 10–15 minutes in both directions, cost Rs 20, take 10–15 minutes.
end of railway line from Colombo, approximately 50 km south following the coastline.
the tourist-friendly beachside town is easily reached by train, bus or tuk-tuk
20 km north following the coast
(districts of Ratnapura, Matara and Galle) is one of the least disturbed and biologically unique lowland rainforest in Sri Lanka. A World Heritage Site since 1989.
(141 km away) has a wide variety of animals living in its beaches, lagoons, freshwater lakes, rivers, enormous rocky outcrops and dense jungle.
Udawalawe National Park where you can spot large herds of Asian elephants, deer and buffalo. It is dry lowland forest, thorny scrub jungle and grassland; several areas of the park have been planted…

cities.d: (Sinhala: යාපනය; Tamil: யாழ்ப்பாணம்) — northern capital. On display is the rich heritage of the Tamil-speaking community.

x.around: Once in Jaffna, there are several modes of transport. The area is rather spread out, so having your own transport would be best.

hidden.d: A bustling market for locally-caught seafood
A small, easy-to-miss museum with a small collection of interesting local history.

An interesting old ruin partly engulfed by trees. This British Governor's residence ("Kachcheri") from the 19th century was left in a state of ruin after the civil war, having been used by both Tamil Tiger and government forces.

x.intro: Jaffna District is the northernmost region of Sri Lanka, and one of the oldest inhabited places on the island. It is populated mainly by Tamil speaking people. The district encompasses Jaffna and its outlying towns, and the quirky and unique islands surrounding it. It is separated from India by the Palk Strait and the Bay of Bengal.

must.d: Beautiful and famous Hindu temple. Come at sunset when the orange coloured temple building is at its most vibrant.
This magnificent library, built in 1933, once housed the largest collection in Asia, with over 97,000 books and rare documents.
A beachside suburb of Jaffna reachable by train or tuk-tuk. It has the port with the ferry to India, Sri Lanka's northernmost railway station, the Keerimalai springs and several temples.

x.safe: Landmines from the civil war might still exist in some places. When walking along the beaches, beware of jellyfish which usually wash up on the beach at dawn. Do not go swimming beyond the floating styrofoam markers.

cities.d: (Sinhala: මහනුවර; Tamil: கண்டி) — spiritual heart of the country, home to a tooth of the Buddha. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

x.around: The local "Three-Wheelers" (Tuk-Tuk) are an amazingly cheap (if you know how to haggle! If you can get them for Rs 60-70 per Km you are doing well) and exciting way of seeing the city, and they run virtually all night long. However, beware of the Tuk-Tuk mafia at the Kandy railway station – they are likely to rip you off (and they threaten Uber or PickMe drivers when they collect passengers near their stand).

hidden.d: The ancient Tea Factory of Hantana Estate located 5 km away from Kandy has been converted into a museum dedicated to the history of Sri Lankan tea, run by the Sri Lanka Tea Board.
The ominipresent Buddha statue seen from everywhere in Kandy city. Take a tuk tuk ride to the Temple or walk, just 1 km away from the Kandy city.
Formerly known as Pitakande Military Cemetery, it is one of the most beautifully landscaped and maintained war cemeteries in the world.
Here lie the remains of several dozen, mostly British, soldiers who died from various causes during the colonial era.

x.intro: Kandy is in the centre of Sri Lanka 125 km away from Colombo and is generally recognised as the island nation's cultural capital. It is on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

must.d: It houses a tooth relic of the Lord Buddha, and is consequently considered one of Sri Lanka's most holy shrines. Although you should expect that you will not be able to view the actual tooth itself, the casket within which it is…
The best botanical garden in Sri Lanka and one of the best in the region. It dates back to the ancient kings of the country although the British changed the look of it.
The second university of Sri Lanka, established in 1942 in affiliation with former 'The University of Ceylon'. This has the largest university library in South Asia which is seven storyed.

Although more an orphanage to make the owners money than a place caring for elephants, it has about seventy semi-tame elephants roaming "freely" around this wonderful sanctuary. Feeding and bathing times are especially enjoyable.
It now houses archeological museum.
Houses an interesting collection of Sri Lankan relics. It is usually quiet and the museum workers are more than happy to provide a free tour.
World's first International Buddhist Museum.

next.d: 72 km north of Kandy, minibus ("A/C bus") No. 43 to Dambulla departing from SWRD Bandaranayake rd (here) before T-junction with Keppeticola st, ticket 470LKR (Oct 2024), at irregular times when seats…
and its forest trails are the most suitable for trekking in Sri Lanka. It has many nature trails cleared through the forest by forest department with campsites.
is 25 km north of Kandy and connected by train
(or stop at Nuwara Eliya or Haputale along the way)

cities.d: (Sinhala: මීගමුව; Tamil: நீர்கொழும்பு) — beautiful landscape and great blue oceans.

x.around: The PickMe app can be used to get a fare estimate, which is usually significantly lower than prices quoted by local drivers.

hidden.d: See where the local fishermen sell their catch of the day. Very busy during the early morning hours.
Built in 1672

x.intro: Negombo is a quiet town in the western coastal area of Sri Lanka, with a tourist strip to the north on Jetwing Beach. Its key attraction is its proximity to the international airport. Formerly the haunt of budget travellers, rising hotel rates and luxury resorts haven't really increased its attractiveness.

next.d: the capital
100 km east of Negombo

x.safe: The main roads and beach areas of Negombo have their share of touts. Expect to be spoken to by taxi drivers, souvenir-sellers and beggars. One man walks the beach with a monkey on a rope, trained to grab hold of tourists' legs.

cities.d: (Sinhala: නුවර එළිය; Tamil: நுவரேலியா) — cool weather, Victorian architecture, top hats, tails and fascinators on race days.

x.around: The town centre is small enough to walk around. To visit sites further afield, take a bus or hire a three-wheeler. A tuktuk within town (e.g. from city center to Pedro Tea Factory) should cost around Rs 700 (2024).

hidden.d: Large man-made lake, along the edge is a beautiful park, with water sports (paddle boats, jet ski rides and cruises) as well as other recreational activities.
Big 108m high waterfall.
A wildlife sanctuary on the edge of town which is great for bird watching. It's also the smallest Sri Lankan National Park and it's quite run down. Very expensive now for foreigners.
Large and impressive, just a short bus journey away. However, it's far smaller and less pretty than Botanical Garden in Kandy.

Offers fascinating tours of a working tea factory. In the hills nearby there are paths through the tea plantations to wander along. You can visit the shop and stroll through the tea fields for free, or hire a guide for a tour.
A beautiful 30-m-high waterfall. Legend has it that a prince and his lover jumped down this waterfall after the king prohibited their love.
Short 5-15 minutes excursion which is followed by a complimentary cup of tea, generally guide asks for a donation in the end.
A picturesque Tudor-style, two-storey red brick building close to the big roundabout at the centre of town. One of the oldest post offices in Sri Lanka and still in use.

x.intro: Nuwara Eliya (pronounced nu-REL-iya) is a city in the Hill Country of Sri Lanka. At 1,868 m (6,129 ft) altitude, the architecture and temperate climate gives it a very different feel from the rest of the country.

must.d: A pleasant place to spend an hour or so, with an astonishing variety of plants, ranging from tropical rain forest to English country garden.

next.d: final station on the railway road
capital
beautiful mountains similar to Nuwara Eliya
offer fascinating walks through this temperate mountain environment, with an 800m vertical drop to be found at World's End.

n.es: Parque nacional de las Llanuras de Horton

intro: Sri Lanka (Sinhala: ශ්‍රී ලංකා Śrī Laṃkā; Tamil: இலங்கை Ilaṅkai), formerly known as Ceylon, is an island in the Indian Ocean, just south of India. It is known for its natural beauty, with stunning beaches all along its coastline, great wildlife and biodiversity, tea plantations, orchards, temples, monuments, and a cultural heritage dating back several millennia.

other.d: (Sinhala: ආරුගම් බොක්ක; Tamil: அறுகம் குடா) – southeast-coast beach town with several top surfing spots

hidden.d: Small boats leave from the southernmost point of the lagoon where local fishermen will take you on a 2-hour tour around the lagoon, showing you eagles, crocodiles, elephants and other animals.

x.intro: Arugam Bay (known locally as Arugam Kudah, often shortened by tourists to "A-Bay") is a town in the Eastern Province of Sri Lanka. It is popular for surfing, and is the location of the only international surf competition in the country.

next.d: (45 km S)

. One daily bus from Pottuvil at 06:00. Rs. 305, 7-8 hours. The bus does not start in Pottuvil. When it arrives in Pottuvil at 06:00-06:30, most seats are taken; you might have to stand for 1-2 hours…
there are buses more or less every hour

other.d: famous for its high red stone fortress and palace ruin, the ancient city of Sigiriya. Nearby, Dambulla with its famous cave temple (both UNESCO World Heritage Sites), and Habarana in close proximity…

x.around: You can organise a tuk tuk to take you around, but it's more exciting just walking around and exploring all the other sights and viewpoints here.

hidden.d: The highest free rock, great for sunsets and sunrises. It also has a water facility building ontop which you can climb on and observe the surrounding plains and often spot elephants or other wildlife.
Foreigners and SAARC citizens will have to buy their tickets here.

It seems like it is only accessible by walking through one of the two resorts that are nearby, but non-guests are allowed through. It has great views of Sigiriya and Pidurangala and a large Buddha statue nearby.
Just south of Sigiriya, even though Pidurangala is hidden from this view.
The first feature one encounters after entering the complex is the water garden. It is an elaborate network of water pavilions, pools, courtyards and water courses.
Some rocks in this garden contain inscriptions recording the names of patrons who donated them to the monks before the arrival of King Kassapa.
This is another rock north of Lion's Rock at almost the same height (340 m), which offers the same awesome views but is much less crowded. The trek uphill takes about 20-30 minutes.

x.intro: ]] Sigiriya is a city in the Central District of Sri Lanka. The "Ancient City of Sigiriya" is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

must.d: The plateau of Sigiriya rock is a lava dome elevated 200 m above the ground (and at a total elevation of 363 m above sea level).

There are two national parks north of Sigiriya, Minneriya and Kaudulla. They are connected through a corridor that enables elephants to roam between the two and depending on the season, they'll mainly stay in one or the other.

n.en: Safari in Minneriya or Kaudulla National Park

next.d: with its great cave temple.
Temple of Tooth
less known place to see elephants in about 20 away from Minneriya
primary place to see elephants in this part of Sri Lanka
take the train from Habarana to this historic, beachside town

x.safe: Bring lots of water as the walk through the gardens and the climb to the top of the rock takes about 1.5 hours. There is no water available inside the complex. It is possible to climb Sigiriya in the rain but care on the stone steps which become slippery when wet. Additionally, the view at the top might get obscured due to the rain.

other.d: (Sinhala: කිතුල්ගල; Tamil: கித்துள்கலை) – known for pristine nature and white-water rafting - 4 hours from Colombo
(Sinhala: මිරිස්ස) – beach village and party hotspot on the south coast close to Matara with two good surfing spots

x.around: Mirissa is a bustling town, you can basically get everywhere on foot or if you are travelling to another beach, by the local bus service which is very regular and inexpensive. The local tuk tuk owners are renowned for attempting to overcharge you. Scooters are becoming more common to rent at most guesthouses. Finding a bicycle to rent is difficult, and the quality is often very poor.
x.intro: Mirissa is a beach and resort town in southern Sri Lanka, near the city of Matara.

other.d: (Sinhala: පාසිකුඩා; Tamil: பாசிக்குடா) – famous beach resort on Sri Lanka's east coast with white sand beaches and upscale hotels
